title: Test disaster recovery plans: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: Which DR test form produces the stated recovery evidence at the lowest justified disruption?
focalInsight: Action taken, production effect, evidence obtained, and acceptance condition for each test type.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: DR Test
nodes.definition: An authorized examination of a DR plan or capability against explicit recovery criteria.
nodes.decision: Select the form only after defining the recovery claim, impact tolerance, participants, and evidence required.
nodes.failureExample: A test with no criteria can complete without proving a business-relevant recovery capability.
nodes.detail: An authorized examination of a DR plan or capability against explicit recovery criteria.

nodes.label: Read Through
nodes.definition: A review in which responsible people read and challenge plan content without rehearsing operational steps.
nodes.decision: Use for completeness, contact, and assumption defects when no behavioral or technical evidence is required.
nodes.failureExample: It cannot establish that people can execute a handoff under time pressure.
nodes.detail: A review in which responsible people read and challenge plan content without rehearsing operational steps.

nodes.label: Walkthrough
nodes.definition: A procedural rehearsal that traces roles and steps through a recovery scenario.
nodes.decision: Use to verify sequencing and ownership before committing alternate systems or production services.
nodes.failureExample: A walkthrough may expose a missing handoff but not a broken replication link.
nodes.detail: A procedural rehearsal that traces roles and steps through a recovery scenario.

nodes.label: Simulation
nodes.definition: A realistic scenario exercise using events or injects to test decisions and coordination without necessarily operating recovery infrastructure.
nodes.decision: Use when leaders need evidence of timely escalation, communication, and decision quality under uncertainty.
nodes.failureExample: A simulation cannot alone prove alternate hardware capacity or backup restorability.
nodes.detail: A realistic scenario exercise using events or injects to test decisions and coordination without necessarily operating recovery infrastructure.

nodes.label: Parallel Test
nodes.definition: A recovery exercise in which alternate capability runs while the production environment remains in service.
nodes.decision: Use for high-value technical proof when parallel resources, safe data handling, and reconciliation are available.
nodes.failureExample: If outputs are not reconciled, parallel processing can mask integrity defects.
nodes.detail: A recovery exercise in which alternate capability runs while the production environment remains in service.

nodes.label: Full Interruption
nodes.definition: A full-scale test that interrupts or transfers normal operations to exercise the real contingency response.
nodes.decision: Use only with executive authority, business consent, defined rollback, and communications because it carries the greatest disruption risk.
nodes.failureExample: A poorly planned interruption creates a real outage that obscures whether recovery would have succeeded.
nodes.detail: A full-scale test that interrupts or transfers normal operations to exercise the real contingency response.

nodes.label: DR Test Evidence
nodes.definition: The objective-linked records—timelines, logs, outputs, decisions, and acceptance sign-off—showing what the DR test established.
nodes.decision: Preserve expected-versus-actual results and unresolved limitations before declaring status.
nodes.failureExample: An attendance list proves participation, not recovery performance.
nodes.detail: The objective-linked records—timelines, logs, outputs, decisions, and acceptance sign-off—showing what the DR test established.

nodes.label: Lessons Learned
nodes.definition: Documented, supported insight from test outcomes that changes recovery plans, capability, or future test design.
nodes.decision: Create lessons after analyzing evidence and route material changes through ownership and controlled maintenance.
nodes.failureExample: Repeating the same exercise without acting on evidence turns testing into ritual.
nodes.detail: Documented, supported insight from test outcomes that changes recovery plans, capability, or future test design.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: Which DR test form produces the stated recovery evidence at the lowest justified disruption?
learningContract.misconception: All DR test labels are interchangeable, or service startup alone proves recovery.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Action taken, production effect, evidence obtained, and acceptance condition for each test type.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: No mandated exercise cadence, vendor design, or numeric recovery target.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: Production must remain available, but the alternate site must run a critical function. Select the test and name the acceptance evidence.
